kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

When generating a .deb file of our Tauri application, we can't currently supply a postinst script. In our case this would be useful for adding our application to the favourites menu, but it has more general utility than that.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like to be able to supply paths to maintainer scripts in my Tauri configuration under the [DebConfig](https://tauri.app/v1/api/config#debconfig) object, and have them be built into the deb.

Example configuration:
```
{
  ...
  "deb": {
    ...
    "maintainerScripts": [
      {
        "name": "postinst",
        "location": "/code/project_name/deb/postinst"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Alternatives considered

Alternative I think is to add the scripts into the deb afterwards, which is a little fiddly and not great DX. E.g.
```
    - cd src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb
    - DEB_FILENAME=$(ls *.deb)
    - ar xv "${DEB_FILENAME}" control.tar.xz

    - mkdir control_untarred
    - tar -xf control.tar.xz -C control_untarred
    - rm control.tar.xz
    - mv ../../../../assets/postinst control_untarred

    - cd control_untarred
    - tar -c *  | xz -z - > control.tar.xz
    - mv control.tar.xz ..
    - cd ..
    - rm -rf control_untarred

    - ar rv "${DEB_FILENAME}" control.tar.xz
    - rm control.tar.xz

    - cd ../../../../..
```
kept_issues.title: [feat] Allow maintainer scripts to be packaged inside a Tauri .deb

Describe the problem

I have a use case where I'd like to be able to detect if the mouse intersects with a tauri window.

The reason is that I use set_ignore_cursor_events(true) to create an overlay displaying something useful to a user.

However, I'd like to be able to allow the user to move their mouse over the window and control the opacity so they can see what behind the window.

Here is an MVP repo that shows you can use javascript to do this but only if the window is in focus.

With Tauri 2.0 hitting beta and bringing Mobile support, one key part of the Mobile (and Desktop) ecosystem is still missing: Widgets.

Right now I'm unaware of any way to write Widgets in Tauri, or even combine an Tauri-based App with e.g. a Swift-based Widget.

While we cannot use Webviews in Widgets, I could imagine a way similar to where Tauri exposes an API and a Widget runtime. 

- The Widget API: Configuration of Layout for the View and data loading that should get run in getSnapshot/getTimeline of the Widget (iOS and macOS is the same)
- The Widget Runtime: Native Swift/Kotlin code that sets up the plumbing and executes what the user has set up in getSnapshot/getTimeline and the view etc

I'm not entirely sure how Scriptable does it, but it seems to expose a minimal set of the Widget API via JavaScript, which lets you do most things. It hasn't been updated to support interactivity yet though (arrived in iOS 17).

I am making a windows bundler and I would like to include the pdb file, but this file is not available until after the build.

The `copy_resources` function happens early before this file is available and will early exit from the build process.

There are a couple PR's that will help with this as pointed out on [discord](https://discord.com/channels/616186924390023171/1239972274040340533/1239972274040340533):

> This one probably would help too but less automatic than 2 ig https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/9734

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like to allow post build resources in the resources bundle configuration, ie files that don't exist yet.

### Alternatives considered

I could write my own nsis template, which I may end up doing, but this is overkill for such a simple matter it seems.

### Additional context

I use the following in my `.cargo/config.toml` file to have rustc make a local pdb file.

```
[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
# By default, the executable embeds absolute path to PDB.
# But that would mean a path on a build machine.
# Instead, we supply a relative path (just the name of the PDB file,
# because we assume it's in the current directory).
rustflags = ["-C", "link-args=/PDBALTPATH:%_PDB%"]
```

### Describe the problem

I missed in the docs (if it's there at all) that plugin names can't have underscores in them. I would have figured this out pretty quickly had the error message for serializing capabilities/default.json been more specific. However, all I got from the build script was
```
thread 'main' panicked at trellis/src-tauri/build.rs:14:6:
  failed to run tauri-build: failed to parse JSON: data did not match any variant of untagged enum CapabilityFile
```

### Describe the solution you'd like

Normally, serde would give a more specific error, but it can't because it doesn't know which variant of the untagged enum to compare the file to. Based on https://github.com/serde-rs/serde/issues/2157#issuecomment-1696114422, this could be mitigated by using https://docs.rs/serde-untagged/latest/serde_untagged/index.html.

I spun up a quick-and-dirty implementation for only `/core/tauri-utils/src/acl/capability.rs`. I'll open a PR for it in a moment, but it obviously needs work. Before it's merged (if it is going in the right direction), we would need to find all similar instances present in other files.

The result is an error like this:
```
  thread 'main' panicked at build.rs:11:6:
  failed to run tauri-build: failed to parse JSON: identifiers can only include lowercase ASCII, hyphens which are not leading or trailing, and a single colon if using a prefix at line 16 column 23
```
It's not perfect; it would also be nice to wrap this error with some information about which file is throwing the error.

Also, it would be nice if the "no underscore" requirement for plugin names is stated in the docs. I think it might go nicely here: https://v2.tauri.app/develop/plugins/, but I don't have time to make another PR.

### Alternatives considered

Besides writing our own deserializer without `serde_untagged`, I don't know of any other options.

### Describe the problem

I am currently updating a large project to Tauri v2, which involves around 100 commands. While doing so, I have encountered a significant amount of boilerplate code that I need to maintain across multiple files. Specifically, for each command, I need to:

- Define the command in the plugin's init functiopatn:
```rs
.invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![auth_get_default_user, auth_set_default_user])
```
- Include the command in `build.rs`:
```rust
.plugin(
    "auth",
        tauri_build::InlinedPlugin::new().commands(&["auth_get_default_user", "auth_set_default_user"]),
)
```
- Allow for usage of my commands in `capabilities.json`: 
```yml
"auth:allow-auth-get-default-user",
"auth:allow-auth-set-default-user"
```
This process is not only repetitive but also makes it challenging to maintain and scale the project. 

### Describe the solution you'd like

Anything that reduces boilerplate, for example:
- New macro that works like `tauri::generate_handler!`, but also generates all permissions
- Allowing for all plugin's commands (for example `plugin:allow-all` or `plugin:allow-*`)

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

I initially discussed this problem on [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/616186924390023171/1251869086980247642)

### Current "sub" problems:
- [ ] There is no `builder.plugins`
- [ ] `InlinedPlugin` requires `&'static [&'static str]` which requires using a lot of `Box::leak`

They implement the plugin trait but are not individual crates following the tauri-plugin- naming scheme, as this would cause circular dependencies for the code depending on tauri and the tauri code depending on the "plugin".

This means currently we:

 Need to reserve/block all tauri-plugin- plugins

 Can not differentiate between core and external plugins

 Describe the solution you'd like

To mitigate some problems we propose a core- prefix for all core plugins and to document and enforce that the core- plugin "namespace" is only able to be used from within the tauri core and not from any other plugin.

- [ ] All tauri-plugin-core- crates should be blocked from being initialized outside of the Tauri core.
- [ ] No tauri-plugin-core crate should be valid. Maybe we reserve the crate name to avoid confusion?
- [ ] The core plugins should be renamed as core- (e.g. core-path, core-window, core-webview, ...).

The documentation should be updated to reflect this behavior.

As this is a breaking change we need to test this explicitly and involve multiple people for a review.
This will add minimal boilerplate in the code and permission files but should be mostly mitigated by having a core:default permission set for all core plugins.

 Alternatives considered

We considered changing the architecture to be able to handle more than one namespace like core:app:reload instead of app:reload but this is also a breaking change involving a bigger refactor and we still have the core prefix/namespace to be reserved.

 Additional context

Was initially discussed with @chippers and @lucasfernog
kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

Currently all Tauri core APIs are pseudo plugins.

They implement the plugin trait but are not individual crates following the `tauri-plugin-` naming scheme, as this would cause circular dependencies for the code depending on tauri and the tauri code depending on the "plugin".

This means currently we:

* Need to reserve/block all tauri-plugin-<core plugin name> plugins

* Can not differentiate between core and external plugins


### Describe the solution you'd like

To mitigate some problems we propose a `core-` prefix for all core plugins and to document and enforce that the `core-` plugin "namespace"  is only able to be used from within the tauri core and not from any other plugin.

- [ ] All `tauri-plugin-core-*` crates should be blocked from being initialized outside of the Tauri core.
- [ ] No `tauri-plugin-core` crate should be valid. Maybe we reserve the crate name to avoid confusion?
- [ ] The core plugins should be renamed as `core-<core-plugin-name>` (e.g. `core-path`, `core-window`, `core-webview`, ...).

The documentation should be updated to reflect this behavior.

As this is a breaking change we need to test this explicitly and involve multiple people for a review.
This will add minimal boilerplate in the code and permission files but should be mostly mitigated by having a `core:default` permission set for all core plugins.

### Alternatives considered

We considered changing the architecture to be able to handle more than one namespace like `core:app:reload` instead of `app:reload` but this is also a breaking change involving a bigger refactor and we still have the `core` prefix/namespace to be reserved.

### Additional context

Was initially discussed with @chippers and @lucasfernog
kept_issues.title: [feat] Tauri Core Plugin Namespace Prefix

### Problems

For running android TV, i found that the Application is fully running without error but wont show up on Android TV os/Google TV os. it turns out android has some more setting to do in their `AndroidManifest.xml`


i think this will nice if tauri generate it for example

### Soultions

based on [Android TV Getting Started](https://developer.android.com/training/tv/get-started/create), there some settings need to be added `Tauri does not generate this things`


on `AndroidManifest.xml`

First :
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">

    <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET" />
    ...other permission...
    <!-- add below setup, after permission before application -->
    <uses-feature android:name="android.software.leanback"
        android:required="false" />

    <application
       ...
```

Secondly:
```xml
<activity
    android:name=".TvActivity"
      ...other setup...
    android:exported="true"
    android:label="@string/your_label">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN" />
        ...i dont set LEANBACK so i comment it...
        <!-- <category android:name="android.intent.category.LEANBACK_LAUNCHER" /> -->
    </intent-filter>
</activity>
```

there is this warning, before upgrade please make sure to check tauri capability.

I was creating a downloader using the tauri-plugin-upload . I want an extra field in the event payload. Which will report the download speed of the file. This field will be updated every second.

Now, why I want this has a strong reason.

I accumulated the progress and run setInterval(() => {}, 1000) to derive the per second download speed of the file. But, I noticed that . Javascript doesn't actually run the setInterval() in every second consistently. Which caused the download speed to show not in a very timely manner.

Describe the problem

tauri-driver lets you specify an application binary path in a platform-neutral manner. It does so by automatically rewriting a neutral WebDriver capability (tauri:options.application) to engine-specific one (e.g., webkitgtk:browserOptions.binary). However, this does not completely abstract away platform differences because you still need to include a file extension (.exe) on Windows and not on other platforms.

 Describe the solution you'd like

tauri-driver could automatically append a platform-specific executable file extension.

 Alternatives considered

Manual edit is possible but has the following downsides:

- If you forget to do this, diagnosing the problem can be hard (some test tools don't print the error, so you need tcpdump to check the error message)
- You need to be careful not to accidentally commit the change to a version control system

Some test tools (e.g., Selenium, WebdriverIO) allow you to programmatically generate WebDriver capabilities. This is not possible on others (e.g., wasm-bindgen-test-runner).

 Additional context

_No response_

Describe the problem

We are developing a Tauri application that requires support for multiple users to log in to the same website simultaneously, each with their own isolated session. While the current data_directory method provides some level of isolation, we are looking for a more granular control over WebView data storage, especially on macOS.

 Describe the solution you'd like

Specifically, we are seeking:

1. A way to create completely isolated WebView instances for each user session, ensuring that cookies, local storage, and other web data do not leak between sessions.

2. On macOS, the ability to leverage WebKit's WKWebsiteDataStore or similar APIs to create truly separate data stores for each WebView instance.

3. A cross-platform solution that maintains Tauri's abstraction layer while providing this enhanced isolation.

This feature would be particularly useful for applications that need to support multiple user accounts, testing environments, or any scenario where complete isolation of web sessions is crucial.

We understand that this might require changes at the wry level or even direct interaction with platform-specific WebView APIs. We're open to discussing the best approach to implement this feature in a way that aligns with Tauri's architecture and future plans.

 Alternatives considered

_No response_

 Additional context

_No response_

### Describe the problem

I aim to run **my Tauri project** as a **Windows service**. To achieve this, I need to use the WiX Util extension, which includes the ServiceInstall element necessary for setting up Windows services.

Here’s the code I am trying to use:
```
<DirectoryRef Id="INSTALLDIR">
...
 <Component Id="Path" Guid="{{path_component_guid}}" Win64="$(var.Win64)">
                <File Id="Path" Source="{{app_exe_source}}" KeyPath="yes" Checksum="yes"/>
                 <ServiceInstall Id="AgentUiServiceInstaller" Type="ownProcess" Vital="yes" Name="GetAppAgentUIService" DisplayName="GetAppAgentUIService" Description="GetApp's Agent UI is running here" Start="demand" Account="LocalSystem" ErrorControl="ignore" Interactive="no">
                    <util:ServiceConfig FirstFailureActionType='restart' SecondFailureActionType='restart' ThirdFailureActionType='restart' RestartServiceDelayInSeconds='60' ResetPeriodInDays='1'/>
                </ServiceInstall>

                <ServiceControl Id="AgentUiServiceControl" Name="GetAppAgentUIService" Stop="both" Remove="uninstall" Start="install" Wait="yes" />
            </Component>
...
</DirectoryRef>
```

## The problem
The current Tauri template does not support adding the WiX Util extension in the main template, so I am attempting to use a custom fragment to include it. However, this workaround has significant limitations:

### 1. Installing the Full Component via Custom Fragment:
The ```.exe``` file cannot be installed directly through the custom fragment because there is no way to reference the ```app_exe_source``` variable within the fragment. The custom fragment does not support accessing bundler variables like ```{{app_exe_source}}```, which limits its usability.

### 2. Installing the Service Without the File Element:
If I attempt to install the service without specifying the file element, there is no way to link the service to the executable file. As a result, the service configuration cannot specify which file to execute when starting the service.


### Describe the solution you'd like

Ideally, there would be two potential solutions, both of which seem to be quite simple to implement::

1. Enable support for the WiX Util extension directly in the main Tauri template, like you doing with the custom fragment.
2. Allow custom fragments to access bundler variables like ```{{app_exe_source}}```, enabling the fragment to correctly reference the ```.exe``` file and establish a link between the service and the executable.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

### Describe the problem

Myself, and especially contributors to a Tauri-based app, do not want/have the signing keys when testing. However, when the various environment variables are not set, the build just fails.

There is no quick way to build a non-signed bundle of an app.

```bash
tauri build --no-sign
```

### Alternatives considered

Currently, the workaround is to have something like a `tauri.conf.dev.json` file with values like:

```json
"bundle": { "windows": null }
```

I just find it odd there is no flag in the cli to disable signing.

It is helpful to go through the whole workflow of installing, manually opening, checking the closing and re-opening behaviour, checking uninstalling (if all expected files are removed). Also, with things like the updater plugin, checking the automated update/restart workflow.

Describe the problem

On Windows, there isn't a way to inspect raw incoming wndproc messages. This is useful in a lot of advanced Win32 API use cases, and is necessary for e.g. the appbar APIs. An appbar is a special window that reserves a portion of the monitor screen space, like the native Windows taskbar. To be properly registered as an appbar, there are several window messages that need to be responded to in a certain way - example of appbar wndproc.

This would also avoid the need for spawning supplementary message windows (e.g. for listening to window events, hardware/device events, etc.).

 Describe the solution you'd like

Perhaps it'd be feasible to expose a new enum member RunEvent::WindowEvent::Raw(u32, usize, isize) (corresponding to msg, wParam, lParam) that could then be used with run_iteration.

 Alternatives considered

 Additional context

_No response_

kept_issues._normalized_body:
Describe the problem

Several platforms supported by Tauri - macOS, iOS, and Android, to name a few - have some kind of built-in push notifications system. For Apple systems, of course there is APNS, and for Android and Firebase-enabled apps, there is FCM.

Tauri isn't yet able to support these APIs, as far as I can tell. On Apple platforms, the developer must register a method with the AppDelegate and call a method on NSApplication, which isn't easy to do from Rust. iOS uses a similar flow, but with UIApplication instead.

Push Notifications are likely to be a common need for Tauri developers, especially on mobile platforms.

 Describe the solution you'd like

I think Tauri should add calls to the UIApplication and/or NSApplication to register for push notification support on behalf of the developer; or, Tauri should make available such calls so the developer can implement support themselves.

 Alternatives considered

1) I looked for plugins and found none
2) I looked for easy Rust bindings to register for APNS, and found none because these APIs use {NS,UI}Application
3) I looked into alternative push systems (3rd-party), but these aren't integrated well with underlying operating systems like Android and iOS, as compared to native push infrastructure

 Additional context

 General support

In most cases, "registering" for these push systems consists of a few relatively simple steps:

1) "Registering" or "requesting" a token from the application, using system APIs, potentially within the app entrypoint
2) "Receiving" the token via some callback or delegate mechanism (the token is typically just some raw bytes or a string)
3) Making the received token available to the developer
 - Usually the developer will want to send this token to a server
 - Callbacks or even just a method to retrieve the latest push token (if any) would work fine for callers, probably

 Apple Platforms

macOS

It looks like tao already sets up an AppDelegate, where we would need to call registerForRemoteNotifications, and then receive the token at the delegate method application(_:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:).

iOS

Nearly identical to macOS, but with UIApplication.registerForRemoteNotifications() and the equivalent delegate method.

 Android

Firebase uses a Service on Android to implement messaging within an app. This service is declared in the AndroidManifest.xml and then implemented within app code; the service:

- Requests a token
- Receives the token/receives updated tokens
- Receives pushed messages directed to the app

This would be implemented in Kotlin as part of an Android mobile plugin for Tauri. Luckily there are no changes anticipated for tao or tauri itself; Android push can happen through the plugin alone.

 Windows

Windows apparently has Windows Notifications System (WNS), which is accessible via the windows crate. So far it appears to function similar to Android, in that a library can obtain a push channel without special code in the app entrypoint.

 Linux

I'm not aware of native push infrastructure for Linux. Other SDKs can be used on Linux which do not require instrumentation in the app entrypoint.
kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

Several platforms supported by Tauri - macOS, iOS, and Android, to name a few - have some kind of built-in push notifications system. For Apple systems, of course there is [APNS](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/registering-your-app-with-apns), and for Android and Firebase-enabled apps, there is [FCM](https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging).

Tauri isn't yet able to support these APIs, as far as I can tell. On Apple platforms, the developer must [register a method with the `AppDelegate` and call a method on `NSApplication`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/registering-your-app-with-apns), which isn't easy to do from Rust. iOS uses a similar flow, but with `UIApplication` instead.

Push Notifications are likely to be a common need for Tauri developers, especially on mobile platforms.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I think Tauri should add calls to the `UIApplication` and/or `NSApplication` to register for push notification support on behalf of the developer; or, Tauri should make available such calls so the developer can implement support themselves.

### Alternatives considered

1) I looked for plugins and found none
2) I looked for easy Rust bindings to register for APNS, and found none because these APIs use `{NS,UI}Application`
3) I looked into alternative push systems (3rd-party), but these aren't integrated well with underlying operating systems like Android and iOS, as compared to native push infrastructure

### Additional context

### General support

In most cases, "registering" for these push systems consists of a few relatively simple steps:

1) "Registering" or "requesting" a token from the application, using system APIs, potentially within the app entrypoint
2) "Receiving" the token via some callback or delegate mechanism (the token is typically just some raw bytes or a string)
3) Making the received token available to the developer
  - Usually the developer will want to send this token to a server
  - Callbacks or even just a method to retrieve the latest push token (if any) would work fine for callers, probably

### Apple Platforms

**macOS**

It looks like [`tao` already sets up an `AppDelegate`](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tao/blob/88f0b4190f77d215f13e88f826c6b5bf06cafe57/src/platform_impl/macos/app_delegate.rs#L103-L107), where we would need to call [`registerForRemoteNotifications`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplication/2967172-registerforremotenotifications), and then receive the token at the delegate method [`application(_:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:)`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplicationdelegate/1428766-application).

**iOS**

Nearly identical to macOS, but with [`UIApplication.registerForRemoteNotifications()`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplication/1623078-registerforremotenotifications) and [the equivalent delegate method](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplicationdelegate/1622958-application).

### Android

Firebase uses a `Service` on Android to implement messaging within an app. This service is declared in the `AndroidManifest.xml` and then implemented within app code; the service:

- Requests a token
- Receives the token/receives updated tokens
- Receives pushed messages directed to the app

This would be implemented in Kotlin as part of an Android mobile plugin for Tauri. Luckily there are no changes anticipated for `tao` or `tauri` itself; Android push can happen through the plugin alone.

### Windows

Windows apparently has [Windows Notifications System (WNS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/windows-app-sdk/notifications/push-notifications/push-quickstart), which is accessible via the [`windows`](https://microsoft.github.io/windows-docs-rs/doc/windows/?search=PushNotifications) crate. So far it appears to function similar to Android, in that a library can obtain a push channel without special code in the app entrypoint.

### Linux

I'm not aware of native push infrastructure for Linux. Other SDKs can be used on Linux which do not require instrumentation in the app entrypoint.
kept_issues.title: [feat] Push Notifications

Describe the problem

It may seem obvious, but it's problematic. Applications like DeepL actually use the Ctrl + c + c shortcut to send text selected from the screen to the application. It's advantageous to use a clipboard because applications can be blocked from selecting text for a number of reasons. As soon as you press Ctrl + c, the data on the clipboard is sent to you so you can take advantage of it.
To implement ctrl + c + c in tauri, ctrl + c must be registered as a shortcut and then implemented by detecting the moment c is pressed within the set time.
However, as soon as you already use ctrl + c for shortcuts, the copy function is not running and the data cannot be utilized for the clipboard.
Can you give me an opinion on how I can implement it in this case?

 Describe the solution you'd like

Even if you register a shortcut such as Ctrl + c, the copy function must be performed. Alternatively, you must be able to register a Ctrl + c + c shortcut.

Describe the problem

Multi-window support via the Window API is not available on iOS. This prevents an application from opening, managing and communicating between multiple windows.

 Describe the solution you'd like

Starting in iPadOS 13, Apple introduced Scenes allowing apps to support multiple UI instances—each representing its own window or scene. A scene is a separate instance of an app's interface managed by a UIWindowScene and handled via its own SceneDelegate. This has been enhanced further in iPadOS 26 by the new windowing system.

Since a scene can host a WKWebView this would allow a Tauri app to create multiple windows on supported devices.

 

 Alternatives considered

N/A

 Additional context

12140 
1580 (WRY)

See article: "Supporting multiple windows on iPad".
kept_issues.body: ### Describe the problem Multi-window support via the [Window API](https://v2.tauri.app/reference/javascript/api/namespacewindow/) is not available on iOS. A scene is a separate instance of an app's interface managed by a `UIWindowScene` and handled via its own `SceneDelegate`. This has been enhanced further in iPadOS 26 by the [new windowing system](https://www.apple.com/uk/newsroom/2025/06/ipados-26-introduces-powerful-new-features-that-push-ipad-even-further/). Since a scene can host a `WKWebView` this would allow a Tauri app to create multiple windows on supported devices. ### Alternatives considered N/A ### Additional context #12140 [#1580 (WRY)](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/issues/1580) See article: ["Supporting multiple windows on iPad"](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/supporting-multiple-windows-on-ipad).

### Describe the problem

Tauri's initialization scripts may not have executed when the webview starts executing user scripts. This can cause Tauri API calls to fail unexpectedly. For example calling `await listen(...)` at a top level will fail if the `__TAURI_INTERNALS__` object has not yet been populated.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like to be able to check if Tauri has finished initializing and wait if it has not. I would suggest a new variable like `window.__TAURI_READY__` or `window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__.ready` which would be set to true after all initialization scripts have finished executing. That could be wrapped in an function in the core library like:

```js
function isReady(): bool {
  return window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__?.ready ?? false;
}
```

Additionally, it would be nice to dispatch an event after the ready flag is set like `window.dispatchEvent("tauriReady", new Event())` so that a script can wait for the ready condition without having to poll.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

See https://discord.com/channels/616186924390023171/1327342177608794113 for discussion.

### Describe the problem

I am implementing `pytauri` Python bindings for the [Emitter](https://docs.rs/tauri/latest/tauri/trait.Emitter.html) trait, but currently, the `Emitter` API is blocking me. Specifically:

In pytauri, the way we handle IPC between Python and the frontend is:

1. On the Python side, we serialize the PyObject to JSON bytes using [pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
2. Use the IPC API provided by Tauri to send the bytes to the frontend.
3. [On the frontend, use `TextEncoder` and `JSON.parse` to parse the bytes into a JSON object](https://github.com/WSH032/pytauri/blob/d19b13e6f5f71eef1a7692b7ebd27e2daefc6e38/crates/tauri-plugin-pytauri/guest-js/src/index.ts#L37-L54).

I have implemented `Channel` and `Command` IPC using this method.

However, for `Emitter`, its `emit*` methods require `payload: Serialize`, and I cannot implement `Serialize` for a [PyObject](https://docs.rs/pyo3/latest/pyo3/type.PyObject.html) without affecting performance.

> Implementing `Serialize` for `PyObject` for serialization is far slower than using `pydantic` for serialization.

---

I noticed that `Emitter` just serializes the `payload` to JSON behind the scenes: <https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/b8eb28877fe822dbe17999fc8af98ed7d0983679/crates/tauri/src/event/mod.rs#L134-L144>.

So, would Tauri accept adding the following method to `Emitter`:

```rust
fn emit_json(&self, event: &str, payload: String) -> Result<()>;
```

This way, I can use pydantic for serialization on the Python side without incurring the [high checking cost](https://github.com/davidhewitt/pythonize/blob/4491cdb46f35ab3fc1b419beef92171fbef510da/src/de.rs#L111-L150).

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add `emit_json_*` series methods

### Alternatives considered

None

### Additional context

This issue is blocking the release of pytauri version 0.2. If Tauri can accept this feature request, I am willing to submit a PR.

Describe the problem

For iOS, Tauri synchronizes both CFBundleVersion and CFBundleShortVersionString with the version property in tauri.conf.json. Android separately defines a versionCode property which is settable in the bundle configuration.

This means we cannot distinguish between the _user-facing_ version visible in stores and the _developer-facing_ build version. Expo for React Native handles this well by defining the following configuration properties:

| Property | Description |
| -------- | ------- |
| version | The user-facing version visible in stores. On Android, it represents versionName name in android/app/build.gradle. On iOS, it represents CFBundleShortVersionString in Info.plist. |
| android.versionCode | The developer-facing build version for Android. It represents versionCode in android/app/build.gradle. |
| ios.buildNumber | The developer-facing build version for iOS. It represents CFBundleVersion in Info.plist. |

 Describe the solution you'd like

Implement a similiar approach in tauri.config.json for defining the _developer-facing_ build version for iOS and macOS.

| `android.versionCode` | The developer-facing build version for Android. It represents `versionCode` in android/app/build.gradle. |
| `ios.buildNumber` | The developer-facing build version for iOS. It represents `CFBundleVersion` in Info.plist. |

I use LLMs a lot to write code but they often struggles to index and parse the latest Tauri docs properly. A lot of the times it starts suggesting code from v1 for example. I would like to be able to add the proper latest docs to the context window or at least create embeddings for it to get better answers and code generation

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add two files, /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt, as described in https://llmstxt.org/, to the Tauri website (something like `tauri.app/llms.txt`):
1. /llms.txt:
    * a summary index in markdown format with key links and project overview.
2. /llms-full.txt
    * markdown file containing the full documentation. this single document would allow llms to index the entire docs in one pass without navigating page-by-page. also useful for llms that have large context windows to just add the full docs as input like a system prompt



### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

other projects have done the same already and it works great! Some examples: https://svelte.dev/docs/llms and https://developers.cloudflare.com/llms.txt

Describe the problem

I’m always frustrated when Tauri applications on macOS do not have a way to gracefully handle app termination requests from the system. Currently, when a user quits the application (via Cmd+Q or pressing the dock icon and then "quit"), the app immediately exits without an opportunity to intercept and prompt the user to save their work or perform cleanup tasks.

 Describe the solution you'd like

I would like Tauri to support the applicationShouldTerminate ( delegate method on macOS. This would allow developers to:

- Intercept termination requests
- Prompt users to confirm quitting or save their work (using dialog plugin)
- Perform cleanup tasks before the app exits
- Potentially delay or cancel termination if needed

And no, ExitRequested event in Tauri does not do this. I'm not sure what that is supposed to do tbh.

kept_issues._normalized_body:
Describe the problem

I'm trying to use Tauri to create a tool that displays key inputs on the desktop. However, if I use a single WebView, it ends up being very large, with most of it being transparent. Despite being transparent, it still captures user input, making a large area unclickable.

As a workaround, I have to use multiple WebViews to render each key separately, but this consumes a lot of memory—each WebView takes around 20-30MB, and the total memory usage could reach approximately 300MB.

I'm wondering if there is a better way to implement this?

 

Allow Tauri windows to be transparent and to pass click events through to underlying windows or the desktop when the click occurs on a transparent area of the window. Specifically, if a user clicks on a part of the window where no pixels are rendered (i.e., the area is fully transparent), the click should not be captured by the Tauri window but instead should affect whatever is beneath it, such as another application or the desktop.

This feature would be particularly useful for applications like:

Desktop widgets (e.g., live2d characters), where the widget overlays the desktop but should not interfere with interactions with other applications beneath it.
Live streaming overlays, such as those displaying chat messages or alerts, where the overlay needs to remain unobtrusive and allow clicks to pass through to the streaming software or other windows.
By supporting click-through on transparent areas, developers can use a single, large webview to cover the required space, rather than relying on multiple smaller webviews. This approach reduces memory usage and simplifies the application's design.

Or is there an API that allows users to determine whether an event is penetrable?

 Describe the solution you'd like

I must admit that this might be so complex that no UI framework seems to support it.

 Alternatives considered

_No response_

 Additional context

_No response_

Describe the problem

With a large and active community, Tauri has accumulated a significant number of open feature requests (currently over 300). While this shows great engagement, it can become challenging to easily gauge which requested features have the broadest community support based on simple indicators like reactions. Manually tracking 👍 reactions across hundreds of issues to identify highly-requested items is time-consuming and difficult to keep up-to-date.

 Describe the solution you'd like

I'd like to suggest using a GitHub Action I created, called Top Issues Action, as a potential way to help visualize this.

What it does:
1. Scans open issues with a specific label (e.g., type: feature request).
2. Counts the number of 👍 (thumbs up) reactions on each of those issues.
3. Generates (or updates) a Markdown file directly in the repository (e.g., POPULAR_FEATURES.md), listing the issues sorted in descending order by reaction count, with links.

Benefits:
 Provides an automated, data-driven overview of features gaining traction via reactions.
 Creates a simple, centralized list for maintainers and the community.
 Requires minimal setup (adding a workflow .yml and a script file to .github).
 Runs entirely within GitHub Actions (free for public repos) using existing issue data.
 It's configurable (label, output file, schedule, commit message, etc.).

This could offer a low-friction way to get a quick pulse check on community interest for different feature ideas.

 Alternatives considered

 Continuing with the current process of manually reviewing issues and discussions.
 Developing a custom internal script or relying on external (potentially paid) project management tools that might offer similar reaction tracking.
 Not implementing any automated ranking based on reactions.

 Additional context

Given the sheer volume of feature requests here, I thought this action might be particularly helpful for the Tauri team and community. I built it as a general tool, but this seems like a prime use case where it could add value by simplifying the discovery of highly-supported suggestions.

You can find the action, full setup instructions, and examples here:
 

Happy to answer any questions if this seems potentially useful for Tauri's workflow!

Describe the problem

By default, Tauri exits when all windows have been destroyed.

AFAIK this is preventable in 2 ways:

1. Call prevent_exit() on RunEvent::ExitRequested events.
 Downside is that it prevents the process from being killed normally. Users have to force kill the app in task manager/activity monitor.
2. Prevent window close via prevent_close and hide windows instead on WindowEvent::CloseRequested.
 Hiding windows comes with side effects and can't be used in all use cases.

Since both approaches come with downsides, it'd be good if there was an intuitive way to keep the process running when all windows are closed. 

---

Source for RunEvent::ExitRequested being called when all windows are closed appears to be here.

 Describe the solution you'd like

Add an additional param on RunEvent::ExitRequested event indicating whether it's due to all windows being closed. Currently it's not possible to discern whether the exit request originated from Tauri itself on window close or legitimate user interaction.

 Alternatives considered

It's definitely hacky but the best solution I've got for now is to run a empty, hidden window in the background to prevent exit. Would love to have a better way of solving this!

 Additional context

_No response_

    <RegistryValue Root="HKCU" Key="Software\..." Name="installed" Type="integer" Value="1" KeyPath="yes" />

data.insert("project_root_path", to_json(std::env::current_dir()?));

Emitting events as well as calling commands requires both TypeScript and the Rust code to agree on magic strings, i.e. the event-listener used on the frontend needs to use the same topic name as the Rust code that emits the event.

This is error prone and only detectable at runtime by running through every code path.

### Describe the solution you'd like

It would be nice Tauri supported something out of the box here.

I've recently adopted `tslink` in our application to compensate for this. For example, with https://github.com/firezone/firezone/pull/9479, we are now exporting constants for all events and routes that the backend and frontend need to agree on. As a result, changing any of the Rust interfaces creates a compile error in TypeScript, making refactorings much safer.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

_No response_

Describe the problem

Currently, the .manage() method provided by the Manager trait requires the managed state to implement 'static, Send, and Sync. This is understandable, since the state is stored globally (e.g., in the AppHandle), and must be accessible throughout the application's lifetime.

However, since Manager is also implemented for Window, it would be logical and useful for developers to associate state specifically with a window's lifetime. That is, when calling .manage() on a Window, the expectation may be that the state is scoped to that window and cleaned up when the window is destroyed — but that’s not currently the case.

This leads to:
- Unnecessary 'static constraints, even when the state only needs to live as long as the window.
- Potential memory leaks or manual cleanup required when tracking per-window state.
- A mismatch between the intuitive use of .manage() on Window and its actual global behavior.

 Describe the solution you'd like

I propose a new method, e.g. .manage_scoped(), that would allow associating state with the lifetime of a specific Window. For example:
 
This would:
- Store the state in a per-window context (not the global AppHandle state map).
- Drop the state automatically when the window is closed or destroyed.
- Be accessible via State in commands invoked from that window.

 Alternatives considered

- Manually managing a HashMap > for window-specific state.
- Using unsafe to extend lifetimes of non-'static types.
For example, when working with wgpu::Surface , I needed to forcibly transmute the lifetime to 'static so I could store it using .manage():
 
While this "works", it’s inherently unsafe and risks undefined behavior if the lifetime assumptions are ever violated.

 Additional context

This feature would be especially useful for apps with multiple windows that each maintain their own independent state, such as document editors, chat clients, dashboards, etc.

It would also make Manager on Window feel more semantically correct — enabling actual per-window management rather than just delegating to the global app state.
kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

Currently, the `.manage()` method provided by the `Manager` trait requires the managed state to implement `'static`, `Send`, and `Sync`. This is understandable, since the state is stored globally (e.g., in the `AppHandle`), and must be accessible throughout the application's lifetime.

However, since `Manager` is also implemented for `Window`, it would be logical and useful for developers to associate state specifically with a window's lifetime. That is, when calling `.manage()` on a `Window`, the expectation may be that the state is scoped to that window and cleaned up when the window is destroyed — but that’s not currently the case.

This leads to:
- Unnecessary `'static` constraints, even when the state only needs to live as long as the window.
- Potential memory leaks or manual cleanup required when tracking per-window state.
- A mismatch between the intuitive use of `.manage()` on `Window` and its actual global behavior.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I propose a new method, e.g. `.manage_scoped()`, that would allow associating state with the lifetime of a specific Window. For example:
```rust
window.manage_scoped(MyState { ... });
```
This would:
- Store the state in a per-window context (not the global `AppHandle` state map).
- Drop the state automatically when the window is closed or destroyed.
- Be accessible via `State<T>` in commands invoked from that window.

### Alternatives considered

- Manually managing a `HashMap<WindowLabel, Arc<...>>` for window-specific state.
- Using unsafe to extend lifetimes of non-`'static` types.
For example, when working with `wgpu::Surface<'_>`, I needed to forcibly transmute the lifetime to `'static` so I could store it using `.manage()`:
```rust
let surface = instance.create_surface(window)?;

// Force the surface to be 'static using unsafe
let surface =
    unsafe { std::mem::transmute::<wgpu::Surface<'_>, wgpu::Surface<'static>>(surface) };
```
While this "works", it’s inherently unsafe and risks undefined behavior if the lifetime assumptions are ever violated.

### Additional context

This feature would be especially useful for apps with multiple windows that each maintain their own independent state, such as document editors, chat clients, dashboards, etc.

It would also make `Manager` on `Window` feel more semantically correct — enabling actual per-window management rather than just delegating to the global app state.
kept_issues.title: [feat] Scoped `manage()` state per window without `'static` lifetime

Describe the problem

Embedding external textures in a webview is a common requirement, such as in video players. I can use web technology to build the UI of a video player, but the video texture being played comes from the output of my own video decoder implementation.

This is a typical example, and there are many more examples where the UI is written using the web, but the actual rendering is done externally.

 Describe the solution you'd like

 1，wry off-screen rendering

wry does not create windows, but instead uses off-screen rendering similar to the cef osr mode. It submits the rendering output of the webview to the application developer for synthesis, and then submits it to tauri for rendering.

 2，Separation of the original window handle and renderer.

Alternatively, application developers can directly obtain the window handle of Tauri and render to the window handle themselves. However, this approach has a drawback: how to prevent the rendering behavior of the WebView from affecting external rendering operations. For example, after the WebView renders, it may overwrite the content rendered directly to the window handle.

 Alternatives considered

First, does wry currently support off-screen rendering? I checked the status of wry, and it seems that off-screen rendering is not fully supported at this time.

If off-screen rendering is not used, is it feasible to render the texture to the wry window handle yourself?

 Additional context

_No response_

There is no documented support for iOS or Android.

 Describe the solution you'd like

 iOS
- Implement UTI (Uniform Type Identifier) registration in Info.plist
- Handle file opening via scene(_:openURLContexts:) from UISceneDelegate)
- Support custom file types and system-defined UTIs
- Handle file opening from external apps i.e. mail and messaging apps

 Android

- Handle file opening via intent handler
- Support custom MIME types and file extensions
- Handle file opening from external apps i.e. mail and messaging apps

kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

Tauri 2.0 includes [file association](https://tauri.app/reference/config/#fileassociation) support for Windows, macOS and Linux. This allows the app to be associated with one or more custom or well-known file types on the platform ([PR 4320](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/4320)).

There is no documented support for iOS or Android.
_Note: There appears be some evidence of [experimental](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/dev/examples/file-associations/src-tauri/src/main.rs) (or partial) support on iOS._

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add file association support for iOS and Android platforms.

#### iOS
- Implement [UTI](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uniformtypeidentifiers) (Uniform Type Identifier) registration in `Info.plist`
- Handle file opening via `scene(_:openURLContexts:)` from [UISceneDelegate](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/UIKit/UISceneDelegate/scene(_:openURLContexts:))
- Support custom file types and system-defined UTIs
- Handle file opening from external apps i.e. mail and messaging apps

#### Android
- Configure [intent](https://developer.android.com/guide/components/intents-filters) filters in `AndroidManifest.xml` for file MIME types
- Handle file opening via intent handler
- Support custom MIME types and file extensions
- Handle file opening from external apps i.e. mail and messaging apps

#### Configuration
- Extend existing file association configuration format in `tauri.conf.json`
- Add mobile-specific configuration options where needed
- Provide Rust + JavaScript API for handling file opening events

### Alternatives considered

N/A

### Additional context

There is currently limited documentation for this feature on desktop.
See community blog [article](https://constantinos.dev/posts/tauri-2-macos-adding-open-with-functionality-to-your-rust-app/).

There may be some overlap with the [deep-link](https://v2.tauri.app/plugin/deep-linking/) plugin which provides support for custom URI schemes.
kept_issues.title: [feat] Add file association support for iOS and Android

kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

Extension of [wry#1587](https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/issues/1587). On iOS Service Workers are disabled in WKWebView by default.

This can be fixed by setting App-Bound Domains for iOS in `Info.plist` in addition to running
`webViewConfiguration.limitsNavigationsToAppBoundDomains = YES;` on the WKWebViewConfiguration object. Then all WKWebViews used in the app are able to use Service Workers [[source](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49673399/service-workers-unavailable-in-wkwebview-in-ios-11-3/64155509#64155509)].

It additionally further locks down the WKWebView to only allow requests to resources from domains which are explicitly whitelisted. That said, I mainly want the feature so I can use a Service Worker in my Tauri App.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I'd like to extend the API in Wry as of (https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/pull/1588) into the WebviewBuilder and the WebviewWindowBuilder structs in Tauri.

### Alternatives considered

I considered using a Tauri plugin; unfortunately the reference to the WKWebviewConfiguration object is not made available to a Tauri plugin, at least as far as I could tell.

### Additional context

App-Bound Domains Blog Post: https://webkit.org/blog/10882/app-bound-domains/
StackOverflow issue about enabling Service Workers in WKWebViews: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49673399/service-workers-unavailable-in-wkwebview-in-ios-11-3/64155509#64155509
kept_issues.title: [feat] Add limit_navigations_to_app_bound_domains into WebviewBuilder and WebviewWindowBuilder

Describe the problem

When switching between different Clash configurations or subscription profiles in Clash Verge, the state of the TUN (enhanced mode) switch in the GUI does not reflect the tun.enable setting defined in the loaded YAML config file. 

This means that even if a configuration explicitly sets tun.enable: true, the TUN mode may remain disabled in the GUI until the user manually toggles it. This causes confusion and inconsistency between the configuration and the actual behavior, especially for users managing multiple profiles with different TUN requirements.

 Describe the solution you'd like

Clash Verge should automatically read the tun.enable value from the loaded config.yaml file and reflect that in the GUI by enabling or disabling the TUN mode accordingly.

Ideally, this should happen:
- When switching between subscription profiles
- When manually loading a new config.yaml file
- On initial startup if a default config is auto-loaded

This would ensure a seamless and consistent experience, especially for advanced users who rely on the tun stack for specific routing behavior (e.g., gVisor for app-level proxying or game optimization).

 Alternatives considered

- Manually toggling the TUN switch every time a profile is loaded (tedious and error-prone)
- Creating separate Clash Verge profiles and remembering to manually adjust TUN mode after switching (unreliable)
- Running Clash or Mihomo manually from command line (not suitable for users who prefer a GUI)

None of these alternatives offer the convenience and consistency that automatic detection from the config file would provide.

 Additional context

- Clash Verge version: 2.3.2
- Kernel: Mihomo
- Platform: [your OS here, e.g. macOS 15.4.1 (24E263) ]

This small enhancement would greatly improve usability for users managing multiple configs with different TUN requirements. Thank you for your continued efforts on this excellent project!

kept_issues.body:
### Describe the problem

# 📌 Feature Request: Add `auto_increment_version_code` option for Android builds

## 📝 Problem

Currently, `versionCode` for Android is written into `tauri.properties` during the build process:

- If `bundle.android.version_code` is set in `tauri.conf.json`, it is always used.  
- Otherwise, Tauri derives `versionCode` deterministically from the semver version (`major*1000000 + minor*1000 + patch`).  

This approach has two main issues:

1. **Google Play requires a strictly increasing integer** for `versionCode`. Repeated builds of the same app version produce the same code, which will be rejected.  
2. Developers must manually bump `bundle.android.version_code` for every release, which is inconvenient for some cases.


### Describe the solution you'd like

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Introduce a new config option under `bundle.android`:

```jsonc
"bundle": {
  "android": {
    "versionCode": 2,                 // manual override (existing)
    "autoIncrementVersionCode": false  // NEW option
  }
}
```

- `false` (default): keep current behavior (manual or semver-derived).  
- `true`: automatically increment `versionCode` on each build by:
  - reading the previous value from `tauri.properties`,
  - incrementing it by `+1`,
  - writing it back for the next build.


------


## ✅ Behavior Summary

| Config setting | Result |
|---|---|
| `bundle.android.versionCode = 123` | Always `123` (explicit override wins) |
| `autoIncrementVersionCode = true` | Increments `versionCode` each build (`1 → 2 → 3 …`) |
| Neither set | Fallback: semver-derived (`major*1000000 + minor*1000 + patch`) |

---

## 🔧 Example

**`tauri.conf.json`**
```json
"bundle": {
  "android": {
    "autoIncrementVersionCode": true
  }
}
```

**Build 1 → `tauri.properties`**
```properties
tauri.android.versionName=1.0.0
tauri.android.versionCode=1
```

**Build 2 → `tauri.properties`**
```properties
tauri.android.versionName=1.0.0
tauri.android.versionCode=2
```

_No response_

### Additional context

Note: I am using a translation tool, so please excuse any awkward expressions.

 Describe the problem
The dialog plugin currently does not implement a folder picker for Android. It seems there was an attempt to implement it in the past, but it failed.

Because, on Android, the only directory picker, Intent.ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE, returns a URI rather than a path.
This causes two problems.

 1. Limitations of Tauri's FS for URIs.
Currently, the Tauri file system API, tauri_plugin_fs, and its JS bindings API can only read and write files, for using a URI. It does not allow listing the contents of a directory or creating new files within a directory from a URI.

 2. Two URIs for one directory
Android defines two distinct URIs for one directory:
1. A URI to access the directory’s own information (e.g., its name, file descriptor).
2. A URI to access the list of child files and subdirectories.

One URI cannot be derived from the other, meaning both must be retained.
But Tauri’s FS path type, tauri_plugin_fs::FsPath, can only hold a single path or URI, creating a conflict.

 Describe the solution

 1. Limitations of Tauri's FS for URIs.
I guess this can be handled effectively by extending the Tauri FS API: just as tauri_plugin_fs::Fs::open can obtain a std::fs::File from a URI, we can add a tauri_plugin::Fs::read_dir function to retrieve a list of URIs for the child files and subdirectories of a given URI.
Similarly, I believe it would be useful to add like createDirAll, createNewFile, removeFile, and removeDir that accept a URI as input and operate.

 2. Two URIs for one directory

To resolve this, I propose defining a new taurifs scheme FS URI to be used internally in Tauri. This URI holds two URIs as its data.
Currently, Android FS URIs are either file:// or content://. The new scheme would add taurifs:// URIs specifically for this purpose.

 Additional context

If this is accepted, I plan to add following in crates/tauri/mobile/android/src/main/java/app/tauri/FsUtils.kt to handle the Custom URIs.

 
 Code 

 
 

After this, the Kotlin-side APIs called by tauri::path::file_name and tauri_plugin_fs::Fs::open will be updated to handle custom URIs. Additionally, new functions such as readDir will be introduced to tauri_plugin_fs to operate directly on URIs. The JS bindings API will also be updated to use these functions internally.

Are these changes acceptable, or is there a better approach?
Thank you :>

Describe the problem

Currently, Tauri provides excellent support for JavaScript frontends and Rust-based backend operations. However, there is no native support for PHP frameworks like CakePHP.

I have implemented a prototype setup where:

- CakePHP runs as a local static PHP build inside a Tauri app
- The frontend runs in the user’s preferred browser (no Tauri frontend)
- Rust/Tauri handles OS-level features, including tray icons, and background tasks

Current limitations:

- There is no native bridge between Tauri/Rust and the PHP frontend, since PHP is not supported in Tauri. Hence, there's no direct communication between Rust and PHP frontend.
- This limits the ability to integrate advanced Tauri features.

 Describe the solution you'd like

Proposed feature: Support for full CakePHP integration with Rust/Frontend bridge in Tauri

Provide a standardized bridge/API in Tauri to enable direct, bi-directional communication between Rust and a local PHP frontend (CakePHP) and run the PHP server inside Tauri's realm (similar to e.g., React with node server).

Support full lifecycle management: starting/stopping PHP server, routing messages/events between Rust and PHP, exposing system features to PHP directly. To do so, static PHP build could be integrated (static-php.dev).

Allow PHP developers to leverage Tauri OS integrations without rewriting the frontend in JS frameworks.

Benefits:

- Enables lightweight, multi-platform PHP desktop apps without Electron/Chromium overhead.
- Makes Tauri a viable option for legacy PHP frameworks like CakePHP (or Laravel, etc.), extending its adoption.
- Allows developers to build full-featured desktop apps using existing PHP expertise.

Missing part: native bridge for direct Rust ↔ PHP communication, which would unlock full potential of Tauri for PHP desktop apps.

 Alternatives considered

It’s more of an idea than a formal feature request. The alternative is my current prototype: Tauri doesn’t have a direct frontend but instead starts PHP and runs CakePHP. The included Rust code handles database synchronization, provides a tray icon, and manages starting and stopping PHP—but there’s no Tauri window.

 Additional context

_No response_

In Electron, applications can listen to system session ending events (shutdown / logout) via app.on('session-end'), and optionally request a short delay to finish critical tasks.

In Tauri, there is currently no documented or official way to:
1. Detect OS-level session termination (shutdown / logout)
2. Distinguish it from normal app exit
3. Request a short grace period to notify frontend or persist state

This is particularly relevant for applications that:
1. Turn off IoT devices
3. Perform final IPC / cleanup
5. Need to mark state consistency before OS termination

 Describe the solution you'd like

Even without guaranteeing full blocking, a minimal API would be helpful, for example:
 
With:
1. Best-effort notification
2. No guarantee of delay
3. Platform-specific implementation where available

This would allow apps to at least:
1. Notify frontend
2. Persist state
3. Gracefully shutdown external connections

Describe the problem

The current state of Tauri does not easily allow users to integrate additional resource files to link against the executable.

The current solution to embed additional resources is to use the embed-resource crate during the build phase to compile and link additional resources. This solution works for most of the cases.

However, the default resource.rc file produced by Tauri includes an ICON definition (which is mandatory for having an app's icon), which prevents including other resources that also contain an ICON declaration due to a linker fatal error about duplicated resources related to the ICON declarations. The current solution is to manually append the desired ICON entry to the resource.rc file generated by Tauri and rebuild it during the build phase.
Another solution may be to add the /TLBID flag to the linker to specify a correct resource ID for the corresponding resource file, but this solution is suboptimal and was not tested. More, the documentation does not mention the content of the resource file generated by Tauri, which may introduce undefined behavior or errors during the build with other resource files.

 Describe the solution you'd like

tauri-winres exposes the append_rc_content method, which allows merging multiple resource files. However, this isn't available via tauri-build nor tauri.conf.json file. One solution would be to allow providing a list of additional resources in the tauri.conf.json file.

 Alternatives considered

Alternatively, allowing multiple icons to be linked against the executable on Windows should also resolve the problem. In this case, adding a note on the documentation on the recommended way of adding additional resources seems a good idea! 

 Additional context

Having multiple icons inside the executable is a standard practice on Windows, notably when adding an entry to the jumplist menu with an alternative icon than the one used by the app executable.

### Describe the problem

The current state of Tauri does not easily allow users to integrate additional resource files to link against the executable.

The current solution to embed additional resources is to use the [`embed-resource`](https://crates.io/crates/embed-resource) crate during the build phase to compile and link additional resources. This solution works for most of the cases.

However, the default resource.rc file produced by Tauri includes an ICON definition (which is mandatory for having an app's icon), which prevents including other resources that also contain an ICON declaration due to a linker fatal error about duplicated resources related to the ICON declarations. The current solution is to manually append the desired ICON entry to the `resource.rc` file generated by Tauri and rebuild it during the build phase.
Another solution may be to add the `/TLBID` flag to the linker to specify a correct resource ID for the corresponding resource file, but this solution is suboptimal and was not tested. More, the documentation does not mention the content of the resource file generated by Tauri, which may introduce undefined behavior or errors during the build with other resource files.

### Describe the solution you'd like

`tauri-winres` exposes the [`append_rc_content`](https://docs.rs/tauri-winres/0.3.5/tauri_winres/struct.WindowsResource.html#method.append_rc_content) method, which allows merging multiple resource files. However, this isn't available via `tauri-build` nor `tauri.conf.json` file. One solution would be to allow providing a list of additional resources in the `tauri.conf.json` file.

### Alternatives considered

Alternatively, allowing multiple icons to be linked against the executable on Windows should also resolve the problem. In this case, adding a note on the documentation on the recommended way of adding additional resources seems a good idea! 

### Additional context

Having multiple icons inside the executable is a standard practice on Windows, notably when adding an entry to the jumplist menu with an alternative icon than the one used by the app executable.

kept_issues.body: ### Describe the problem # 16KB Page Size Support for Tauri Android Apps ## The Problem When building a Tauri Android app that targets Android 15+ (API 35+), Google Play requires 16KB page size support starting November 1, 2025. ### Symptoms 1. **AAB metadata shows correct alignment:** ```bash java -jar bundletool-all-1.18.3.jar dump config --bundle=app.aab | grep alignment # Output: "alignment": "PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K" ✅ ``` 2. **But native libraries (.so files) have wrong alignment:** ```bash llvm-objdump -p libRaPiMATE_lib.so | grep LOAD # Output: LOAD off ... align 2**12 ❌ (4KB instead of 16KB) ``` 3. **App runs in compatibility mode on 16KB devices** with performance penalties. ### Root Cause **Tauri's build system overrides `.cargo/config.toml` rustflags**, so the standard Rust approach of adding linker flags to cargo configuration doesn't work. The flags need to be injected via `build.rs` instead. ### Describe the solution you'd like ### Step 1: Update Gradle Configuration Edit `src-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts`: ```kotlin android { // Specify NDK r28+ for automatic 16KB support ndkVersion = "28.0.12433566" packaging { jniLibs { // Enable uncompressed native libraries with 16KB alignment useLegacyPackaging = false } } } ``` **Requirements:** - Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) >= 8.5.1 - NDK >= r28 ### Step 2: Configure Rust Linker Flags Edit `src-tauri/build.rs`: ```rust fn main() { let target = std::env::var("TARGET").unwrap_or_default(); if target.contains("android") { // Both flags are required for proper 16KB alignment println!("cargo:rustc-link-arg=-Wl,-z,max-page-size=16384"); println!("cargo:rustc-link-arg=-Wl,-z,common-page-size=16384"); } tauri_build::build() } ``` **Why `build.rs` and not `.cargo/config.toml`?** Tauri's build system ignores rustflags in `.cargo/config.toml`. The `println!` statements in `build.rs` inject linker arguments directly into the compilation process, which Tauri respects. ### Step 3: Clean and Rebuild ```bash # Clean all previous build artifacts cd src-tauri cargo clean cd .. # Rebuild the AAB with 16KB support npm run tauri android build -- --aab ``` ### Step 4: Verify the Fix **Check AAB metadata:** ```bash java -jar bundletool-all-1.18.3.jar dump config \ --bundle=src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/outputs/bundle/universalRelease/app-universal-release.aab \ | grep alignment ``` Expected output: `"alignment": "PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K"` **Verify native library alignment:** ```bash # Extract the AAB cd /tmp mkdir test_16kb unzip /path/to/app-universal-release.aab -d test_16kb # Check ARM64 library alignment $ANDROID_HOME/ndk/28.0.12433566/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/llvm-objdump \ -p test_16kb/base/lib/arm64-v8a/libRaPiMATE_lib.so \ | grep "LOAD" | head -3 ``` Expected output: ``` LOAD off 0x0000000000000000 vaddr 0x0000000000000000 paddr 0x0000000000000000 align 2**14 LOAD off 0x00000000003251b0 vaddr 0x00000000003291b0 paddr 0x00000000003291b0 align 2**14 LOAD off 0x000000000065a780 vaddr 0x0000000000662780 paddr 0x0000000000662780 align 2**14 ``` **Note:** `2**14 = 16384` (16KB alignment) ✅ --- ## Testing on 16KB Emulator (Optional) ### Create 16KB Emulator 1. Open Android Studio SDK Manager 2. Go to **SDK Platforms** tab 3. Check "Show Package Details" 4. Select: **Google APIs Experimental 16 KB Page Size ARM 64 v8a** 5. Click "Apply" to download ### Create Virtual Device ```bash # List available system images $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager --list | grep "16 KB" # Create AVD with 16KB page size $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/avdmanager create avd \ -n "Pixel_9_16KB" \ -k "system-images;android-35;google_apis_16k;arm64-v8a" \ -d "pixel_9_pro" # Launch emulator $ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator -avd Pixel_9_16KB ``` ### Verify Emulator Configuration ```bash # Should return 16384 adb shell getconf PAGE_SIZE ``` ### Install and Test ```bash # Generate APKs from AAB java -jar bundletool-all-1.18.3.jar build-apks \ --bundle=app-universal-release.aab \ --output=rapimate.apks \ --mode=universal # Extract universal APK unzip rapimate.apks -d apks/ # Install on device/emulator adb install apks/universal.apk ``` Check logcat for any warnings: ```bash adb logcat | grep -i "page\|compat" ``` If properly configured, there should be **no warnings** about "page size compat mode". --- ## Summary The fix requires **two levels of alignment**: 1. **ZIP-level alignment** (via AGP): Ensures AAB metadata shows `PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K` 2. **ELF-level alignment** (via linker flags): Ensures `.so` files have `align 2**14` For Tauri apps specifically, linker flags **must** be set in `build.rs` using `println!("cargo:rustc-link-arg=...")` because Tauri overrides `.cargo/config.toml`. --- ## References - [Android 16KB Page Sizes Guide](https://developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes) - [Google Play Requirements](https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2025/05/prepare-play-apps-for-devices-with-16kb-page-size.html) ### Alternatives considered _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_

kept_issues._normalized_body:
Describe the problem

Today, Tauri apps rely on:

 A WebView system (WebKitGTK, WKWebView, WebView2) via WRY
 Running JavaScript inside this WebView
 IPC based on HTTP interception or message bridges (which is not very clean)

This architecture introduces several structural limitations:

1. The JavaScript runtime environment is closely coupled to the WebView system.
2. Communication relies on intercepted layers of HTTP or WebView messaging.
3. The rendering engine varies between platforms.
4. Applications must integrate execution logic into the WebView sandbox.
5. API availability differs between operating systems.
6. There is no direct integration with modern standalone JS runtimes (Node, Deno, Bun).
7. Responsive frameworks create a server that is intercepted by Tauri and opened in a webview window.

This prevents:

 Using system-level JavaScript runtime environments and using packets relating to this runtime.
 Have a consistent rendering engine across all platforms.
 Deep runtime synchronization between JS memory, Rust memory (and WASM).
 Cleaner and structured IPC (e.g. protobuf instead of HTTP interception).

The current model works well, but it inherits the structural constraints of the system's WebView abstraction that limit performance and restrict some limitations for developers like me.

 Describe the solution you'd like

 Native JS Runtime Integration (Node/Deno/Bun) + Servo Engine + Protobuf-Based Reactive DOM Synchronization

I propose a next generation architecture for Tauri v3 built around the following principles:

 1. Replace the WebView-based JS execution with an external JS runtime

Instead of running JavaScript in WebView:

 Tauri runs JavaScript in a runtime environment installed by the system (Node, Deno, Bun).
 The runtime communicates with the rendering engine via Protobuf via in-memory transport.
 No HTTP interception layer is used.
 No fake local server.
 No WebView message bridge.
 Add an option to automatically convert http servers into buffer protocols (useful for graphics libs that have not had time to be patched)

This transforms the JS runtime environment into a first-class runtime environment.

Tauri should therefore expose a library to the javascript runtime which brings all the webAPIs via protocol buffers for synchronization with the display (explained in more detail in point ...)

---

 2. Replacing Tao with Winit:

Use the "winit" solution as a window/event backend because it now has everything it was missing when you created its fork called Tao and it is more flexible, allowing for more advanced integration (like keyboards which are still experimental on Tao while being complete on Winit)

---

 3. Replace WRY/WebView with Servo

Instead of relying on system WebViews:

 Use Servo as a cross-platform rendering engine.
 Install Servo as a system dependency (like WebKitGTK).
 Do not integrate Chromium type motors per application (no Electron style duplication).
 Use Servo's native Rust API as well as protobuf for communication.

Advantages:

 Unified engine on all platforms
 Modern architecture, based on Rust and secure
 Full control over web APIs and allows you to expose the js runtime APIs to the web engine or even synchronization as explained below.
 Deterministic behavior

---

 4. Expose Servo Web APIs to the JS runtime environment via Protobuf

The JS runtime (Node/Deno/Bun) interacts with Servo via structured links:

 Interface based on Protobuf
 No HTTP
 No DOM chain injection
 Direct API mapping

Servo acts as a rendering engine.
The JS runtime acts as the logic engine.
Protobuf synchronizes the apis, functions, classes, objects, etc. between the servo js and the runtime (via api written in rust then compiled in .proto via protocol compiler then loaded in js via protobuf runtime).

---

 5. Virtual DOM synchronization via reactive signals

Frames like:

 Fresh
 React
 Other responsive libraries

can run on a virtual DOM (which already exists in Deno internally, even if not rendered).

Architecture:

 Reactive state changes trigger fine-grained signals (like in Leptos, possible to fork some of their work to implement this).
 These signals produce structured updates of DOM differences.
 Updates will, in our case, be serialized via Protobuf.
 Servo receives targeted DOM patch operations that can be injected natively via external embeding rust without duplication.
 No complete rendering.
 No HTTP loop.
 No browser type document reloading.
 Possibility of doing hot reload when the project is Tauri run and not compiled.

This gives:

 Deterministic DOM synchronization
 Minimum update area
 Clear separation between the runtime environment and the rendering engine
 Contribution of modern apis systems to javascript
 The rust system remains identical from the point of view of the developer using Tauri although the communication method has changed

---

 6. Shared memory model

Introduce:

 Synchronization of WASM linear memory with native rust memory
 Complete mapping of JS execution memory for interoperability between Rust-RuntimeJS-JSdansServo
 Rust integration layer mapping
 And more

Use:

 Protobuf for structured messaging
 Memory shared securely
 Hot reloading mechanisms similar to Dart

This allows:

 Deep Rust–WASM–JS integration
 Effective state propagation
 Advanced development tools

---

 7. Dependencies installed on the system (no integration per application)

To avoid Electron type bloating:

 Deno/Node/Bun installed system-wide
 Servo installed system-wide
 Winit as Rust dependency

Applications depend on system libraries via GObject introspection to have to code the same regardless of the operating system targeted.

Supported platforms:

 Linux
 macOS
 Windows
 Android
 iOS

This maintains a small application size while improving the execution speed and capabilities offered by Tauri.

 Alternatives considered

1. Continue using system WebViews
 → Keeps platform inconsistency and limited runtime integration.

2. Embed Chromium (Electron-like)
 → Too heavy, duplicates engine per application.

3. Keep current Tauri architecture but improve IPC
 → Improves ergonomics but not architectural limitations.

4. WASM-only frontend
 → Still requires a rendering engine and JS host.

The proposed architecture removes WebView as the execution container and separates:

 Rendering engine (Servo)
 Runtime engine (Node/Deno/Bun)
 Window system (Winit)

This creates a cleaner, more modular design.

 Additional context

This proposal aims to position Tauri as:

 A native Rust-first and JavaScript application framework
 A Rust and Javascript library that synchronizes them with each other and with Servo
 A deterministic and extensible rendering platform
 A modern alternative to Electron without incorporating chrome

The current WebView-based model is pragmatic, but an external Servo + JS engine runtime architecture could enable:

 Better access to the operating system while remaining compatible with all bones
 Predictable and extensible behavior
 Better performance
 Advanced status synchronization
 Deeper integration of Rust/JS(/WASM optional)

This would be an important architectural development which in my opinion represents what v3 of Tauri should be.

I understand this would be a significant change and potentially part of a long-term roadmap, but I think it fits with Tauri's philosophy of performance, security, and native control of Rust.

Furthermore, before making this proposal I made sure that it was entirely possible although complicated and I am obviously prepared to contribute greatly to the code if my proposal were to be accepted.
